claims.text: The proposed model independently treats lattice and electronic heat transport.
Incorporating effective-temperature scaling of lattice distortions will reduce lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error.
The applicable initial material is single-phase bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The applicable HfNbTaTiZr material contains 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model is applicable from approximately 100 K to 1200 K.
The stated temperature range can be studied while maintaining minimal extrinsic defect formation.
Variations in atomic radii produce static lattice distortions through variations in interatomic separation.
Thermal fluctuations produce dynamic lattice distortions.
The effects of static and dynamic lattice distortions can be unified through an effective-temperature scaling law.
Effective temperature directly scales the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local lattice distortions influence conductivity.
Separately treating lattice vibrations and electronic transport improves prediction of lattice thermal conductivity.
Decoupling lattice and electronic transport eliminates an error inherent in earlier analytical estimates.
The model will predict lattice thermal conductivity with an error of approximately 30% or less.
The model will match experimental trends both below 200 K and from 300 K to 1200 K.
Earlier defect-free bulk approaches conflate lattice and electronic transport and can have prediction errors exceeding 50%.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below 200 K.
HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen has a total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 K to 1200 K.
Phase separation and non-equilibrium microstructures introduce additional scattering mechanisms that may invalidate the predicted improvement.
Quantum effects become prominent below 100 K and may reduce model accuracy.

contradictions.description: The target state is specified as containing 1 wt.% oxygen, whereas the falsification experiment calls for high-purity samples without stating that the same oxygen level will be retained. This makes the validation sample population inconsistent or ambiguous.

The hypothesis requires evaluation of lattice conductivity separately from electronic transport, but the claimed high-temperature agreement is framed against a baseline observation of total conductivity. Total conductivity cannot by itself establish agreement of the predicted lattice component.
